candidates.title: Efficient Attention Mechanisms for Scaling Large Language Models on Resource Constrained Devices
candidates.venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy Systems and Power Engineering (EESPE)
candidates.abstract: Large language models such as LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen have achieved strong performance across a wide range of natural language understanding and generation tasks. However, their deployment on resource constrained devices, including mobile phones, edge servers, and embedded accelerators, remains limited by the high computational and memory costs of standard self attention. This limitation is particularly relevant to modern electronics and power systems, where on device natural language interfaces, equipment maintenance log analysis, and edge side dispatch assistants require low latency inference without continuous dependence on remote datacenters.To address this challenge, this study proposes a hybrid efficient attention framework for autoregressive decoding on commodity edge hardware. The proposed framework integrates block sparse linear attention, grouped query attention, and low bit key value cache quantization within a unified architecture. Specifically, the method replaces dense softmax attention with an efficient kernelized approximation, adopts a structured band plus global sparsity pattern to retain both local context and long range dependencies, shares key and value projections across attention heads to reduce cache size, and stores cached activations using four bit group wise quantization with fused dequantization during attention computation. To ensure stable adaptation, the compressed student model is fine tuned using a training objective that combines cross entropy supervision with layer wise feature distillation from a full precision dense attention teacher.Experiments on WikiText 103 and LongBench using a seven billion parameter backbone show that the proposed framework reduces key value cache memory by 6.3 times and improves end to end decoding latency by 2.4 times on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX platform, while increasing perplexity by only 0.31 compared with the full precision dense attention baseline. A case study on a power equipment maintenance log dataset further demonstrates that the compressed student model retains more than 96 percent of the dense teacher accuracy in fault category classification under a 25 W thermal envelope. These results indicate that carefully designed approximate attention mechanisms can substantially improve the deployability of large language models on edge devices while preserving their core modeling capability.
candidates.reason: 資源制約デバイス上の自己回帰デコード向けに、ブロック疎線形注意・グループ化クエリ注意・低ビットKVキャッシュ量子化を統合したハイブリッド効率注意を提案しており、オンデバイス推論の注意・KV機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Voltron: Enabling Elastic Multi-Device Execution of LLM Inference for Empowered Edge Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used in intelligent services due to their remarkable capability in generative tasks. Typically, LLM-based services process the inference requests of the users in a centralized data center. Unfortunately, such centralized execution has limitations for end-users, such as increased response latency with communication overhead and privacy leakage risk. To alleviate the aforementioned limitations, there have been increasing pushes to execute LLM inference locally on user-end devices. However, the limited resources of a single edge device impose restrictions on achievable accuracy of LLMs. To overcome the issue, we first propose to leverage multiple user-end devices available at the edge for LLM inference, enabling the execution of larger models. Specifically, we propose Voltron, a novel on-device LLM inference framework that elastically utilizes multiple user-end devices for LLM inference execution while adapting to diverse real-world edge environments. In our evaluation, Voltron achieves up to 16.5% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art LLMs that can be executed on a single edge device, satisfying user QoS requirements.
candidates.reason: 複数ユーザーデバイスへLLM推論を弾力的に分散し環境変化へ適応するVoltronは、単一エッジデバイスの資源制約を超えて大規模モデルを実行するオンデバイス推論基盤への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: TrimMoE A communication aware and adaptive depth framework for distributed edge inference
candidates.abstract: Serving Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models across distributed edge servers is bottlenecked by the cross-server expert transmission. The existing approaches mainly focus on how to reach a remote expert faster. However, in this paper, we instead consider whether a given layer, and the layers after it, need to be executed at all. To this end, a communication-aware adaptive-depth framework is proposed in this paper, termed TrimMoE, which couples layer skipping and confidence-based early exit with substitute execution and server-expert selection under a unified quality budget. Specifically, in the offline stage, TrimMoE freezes the backbone, trains the lightweight per-layer exit heads, calibrates the per-layer importance thresholds, and allocates the expert replicas by a skip/exit-aware redundancy benefit. In the online stage, a transition-aware look-ahead anticipates the token movement, so that the depth reduction targets the costliest transmissions, and besides, two feedback rules adapt the delay-quality weights and the exit threshold. Moreover, we prove that the substitution-and-skipping proxy degradation never exceeds the configured budget, and that the early exit is admitted only under a calibrated confidence gate. On a heterogeneous 10-server testbed with Switch-Base-8E, Qwen-MoE-A2.7B, and Mixtral-8x7B, TrimMoE reduces the average latency by up to 62.8%, lowers the cross-server traffic and the remote-execution ratio, and sustains high throughput under load, while keeping the task-quality degradation within a 2% bound.
candidates.reason: 分散エッジサーバ間でMoEをサービングする際、層スキップと確信度早期終了、代替実行と専門家配置を品質予算の下で統合するTrimMoEは、跨サーバ専門家転送を減らす推論機構への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Semantic-Aware Multi-LoRA Orchestration in Edge Federation: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Optimization Under QoE Constraints
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
candidates.abstract: The rapid scaling of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven the adoption of Multi-LoRA as a lightweight mechanism for model customization. However, deploying Multi-LoRA in edge federations introduces significant challenges in operational expenditure (OPEX) and latency efficiency. In this paper, we introduce a semantic-aware Multi-LoRA serving framework for edge federations that jointly optimizes OPEX and Quality of Experience (QoE). Specifically, we propose a semantic compatibility model based on behavioral embeddings to enable high-fidelity LoRA substitution, thereby reducing cold-start latency and redundant cross-region data transfers. We further develop a hierarchical multi-timescale architecture that separates long-term model provisioning from real-time request dispatching, allowing the system to adapt to dynamic workload skewness under data sovereignty constraints. Additionally, we design a Lyapunov-based dynamic dispatching algorithm to jointly optimize cross-cluster routing, node auto-scaling, and VRAM execution modes in real time. Extensive discrete-event simulations based on real-world Microsoft Azure Functions traces demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly mitigates the batch-squeezing effect and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in steady-state throughput, long-term OPEX reduction, and 95th-percentile Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) Service Level Objective (SLO) compliance.
candidates.reason: エッジ連合でのMulti-LoRAサービングに意味的互換モデルによるLoRA代替、長期プロビジョニングと実時間ディスパッチの分離、Lyapunov型動的振り分けを導入し運用費とQoEを最適化しており、LoRAサービング基盤への直接貢献である。

candidates.title: Improving the Performance of Out-of-Core LLM Inference Using Heterogeneous Host Memory
candidates.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Workload Characterization
candidates.abstract: The memory footprint of modern applications like large language models (LLMs) far exceeds the memory capacity of accelerators they run on and often spills over to host memory. As model sizes continue to grow, DRAM-based memory is no longer sufficient to contain these models, resulting in further spill-over to storage and necessitating the use of technologies like Intel Optane and CXL-enabled memory expansion. While such technologies provide more capacity, their higher latency and lower bandwidth has given rise to heterogeneous memory configurations that attempt to strike a balance between capacity and performance. This paper evaluates the impact of such memory configurations on a GPU running out-of-core LLMs. Starting with basic host/device bandwidth measurements using an Optane and Nvidia A100 equipped NUMA system, we present a comprehensive performance analysis of serving OPT-30B and OPT-175B models using FlexGen, a state-of-the-art serving framework.Our characterization shows that FlexGen’s weight placement algorithm is a key bottleneck limiting performance. Based on this observation, we evaluate two alternate weight placement strategies, one each optimizing for inference latency and throughput. When combined with model quantization, our strategies improve latency and throughput by 27% and 5x, respectively. These figures are within 9% and 6% of an all-DRAM system, demonstrating how careful data placement can effectively enable the substitution of DRAM with high-capacity but slower memory, improving overall system energy efficiency.
candidates.reason: OptaneやCXLで拡張した異種ホストメモリ上でFlexGenによるOPT-30B／175Bのアウトオブコア推論を実測し、メモリ構成がサービング性能へ与える影響を包括的に示しており、オフロード推論の計測として直接貢献がある。
